-- | Identifies a JavaScript execution context. When using GHCJS this is
--   just <tt>()</tt> since their is only one context. When using GHC it
--   includes the functions JSaddle needs to communicate with the
--   JavaScript context.
data JSContextRef

-- | The <a>JSM</a> monad keeps track of the JavaScript execution context.
--   
--   When using GHCJS it is <a>IO</a>.
--   
--   Given a <a>JSM</a> function and a <a>JSContextRef</a> you can run the
--   function like this...
--   
--   <pre>
--   runJSM jsmFunction javaScriptContext
--   </pre>
data JSM a

-- | Gets the JavaScript context from the monad
askJSM :: MonadJSM m => m JSContextRef

-- | Runs a <a>JSM</a> JavaScript function in a given JavaScript context.
runJSM :: MonadIO m => JSM a -> JSContextRef -> m a

-- | The <a>MonadJSM</a> is to <a>JSM</a> what <a>MonadIO</a> is to
--   <a>IO</a>. When using GHCJS it is <a>MonadIO</a>.
class (Applicative m, MonadIO m) => MonadJSM (m :: Type -> Type)
liftJSM' :: MonadJSM m => JSM a -> m a
($dmliftJSM') :: forall (m' :: Type -> Type) (t :: (Type -> Type) -> Type -> Type) a. (MonadJSM m, MonadJSM m', MonadTrans t, m ~ t m') => JSM a -> m a

-- | The <a>liftJSM</a> is to <a>JSM</a> what <a>liftIO</a> is to
--   <a>IO</a>. When using GHCJS it is <a>liftIO</a>.
liftJSM :: MonadJSM m => JSM a -> m a

-- | This is the same as <a>JSContextRef</a> except when using
--   ghcjs-dom-webkit with GHC (instead of ghcjs-dom-jsaddle)
type DOMContext = JSContextRef

-- | This is the same as <a>JSM</a> except when using ghcjs-dom-webkit with
--   GHC (instead of ghcjs-dom-jsaddle)
type DOM = JSM

-- | This is the same as <a>askJSM</a> except when using ghcjs-dom-webkit
--   with GHC (instead of ghcjs-dom-jsaddle)
askDOM :: MonadDOM m => m DOMContext

-- | This is the same as <a>runJSM</a> except when using ghcjs-dom-webkit
--   with GHC (instead of ghcjs-dom-jsaddle)
runDOM :: MonadIO m => DOM a -> DOMContext -> m a

-- | This is the same as <a>MonadJSM</a> except when using ghcjs-dom-webkit
--   with GHC (instead of ghcjs-dom-jsaddle)
type MonadDOM = MonadJSM

-- | This is the same as <a>liftJSM</a> except when using ghcjs-dom-webkit
--   with GHC (instead of ghcjs-dom-jsaddle)
liftDOM :: MonadDOM m => DOM a -> m a

-- | Safe but slow way to cast
--   
--   <pre>
--   castTo Element x &gt;&gt;= \case
--       Nothing      -&gt; error "Was not an element"
--       Just element -&gt; ...
--   </pre>
castTo :: (Coercible obj JSVal, IsGObject obj', MonadJSM m) => (JSVal -> obj') -> obj -> m (Maybe obj')

-- | Unsafe way to cast. Slow but if it fails an error message will result
--   and the message should be clear (uses HasCallStack).
--   
--   <pre>
--   element &lt;- unsafeCastTo Element x
--   </pre>
unsafeCastTo :: (HasCallStack, Coercible obj JSVal, IsGObject obj', MonadJSM m) => (JSVal -> obj') -> obj -> m obj'

-- | Unsafe way to cast. Fast but if it fails you program will probably
--   crash later on in some unpredictable way.
--   
--   <pre>
--   element &lt;- uncheckedCastTo Element x
--   </pre>
uncheckedCastTo :: (Coercible obj JSVal, IsGObject obj') => (JSVal -> obj') -> obj -> obj'

-- | <a>EventM</a> provides a convenient monadic interface for handling DOM
--   events.
--   
--   The <a>DOM Event interface</a> is exposed, as well as functions for
--   accessing UIEvents and MouseEvents.
module JSDOM.EventM

-- | <tt>IO</tt> with the current <tt>Event</tt> in scope (read with
--   <a>event</a>).
type EventM t e = ReaderT e DOM
newtype SaferEventListener t e
SaferEventListener :: Function -> SaferEventListener t e
data EventName t e

-- | See <a>eventListenerNew</a>.
newListener :: IsEvent e => EventM t e () -> DOM (SaferEventListener t e)

-- | See <a>eventListenerNewSync</a>.
newListenerSync :: IsEvent e => EventM t e () -> DOM (SaferEventListener t e)

-- | See <a>eventListenerNewAsync</a>.
newListenerAsync :: IsEvent e => EventM t e () -> DOM (SaferEventListener t e)

-- | Add an EventListener to an EventTarget.
addListener :: (IsEventTarget t, IsEvent e) => t -> EventName t e -> SaferEventListener t e -> Bool -> DOM ()

-- | Remove an EventListener from an EventTarget.
removeListener :: (IsEventTarget t, IsEvent e) => t -> EventName t e -> SaferEventListener t e -> Bool -> DOM ()

-- | Release the listener (deallocates callbacks).
releaseListener :: (IsEventTarget t, IsEvent e) => SaferEventListener t e -> DOM ()

-- | Shortcut for create, add and release:
--   
--   <pre>
--   releaseAction &lt;- on element <a>click</a> $ do
--       w &lt;- <a>currentWindowUnchecked</a>
--       <a>alert</a> w "I was clicked!"
--   -- remove click handler again
--   releaseAction
--   </pre>
on :: (IsEventTarget t, IsEvent e) => t -> EventName t e -> EventM t e () -> DOM (DOM ())

-- | Like <a>on</a> but always uses <a>newListenerSync</a>
onSync :: (IsEventTarget t, IsEvent e) => t -> EventName t e -> EventM t e () -> DOM (DOM ())

-- | Like <a>on</a> but always uses <a>newListenerAsync</a>
onAsync :: (IsEventTarget t, IsEvent e) => t -> EventName t e -> EventM t e () -> JSM (JSM ())

-- | <a>onSync</a> for multiple targets &amp; events.
--   
--   The returned <tt>IO</tt> action removes them all at once.
onTheseSync :: (IsEventTarget t, IsEvent e) => [(t, EventName t e)] -> EventM t e () -> DOM (DOM ())

-- | <a>onAsync</a> for multiple targets &amp; events.
--   
--   The returned <tt>IO</tt> action removes them all at once.
onTheseAsync :: (IsEventTarget t, IsEvent e) => [(t, EventName t e)] -> EventM t e () -> DOM (DOM ())
event :: EventM t e e
eventTarget :: IsEvent e => EventM t e (Maybe EventTarget)
target :: (IsEvent e, IsGObject t) => EventM t e (Maybe t)

getReturnValue :: IsEvent e => EventM t e Bool

uiView :: IsUIEvent e => EventM t e Window

module JSDOM
globalThis :: MonadDOM m => m (Maybe GlobalThis)
globalThisUnchecked :: MonadDOM m => m GlobalThis
currentWindow :: MonadDOM m => m (Maybe Window)
currentWindowUnchecked :: MonadDOM m => m Window
currentDocument :: MonadDOM m => m (Maybe Document)
currentDocumentUnchecked :: MonadDOM m => m Document

-- | Forces execution of pending asyncronous code
syncPoint :: JSM ()

-- | Forces execution of pending asyncronous code after performing
--   <tt>f</tt>
syncAfter :: JSM a -> JSM a

-- | On GHCJS this is <a>waitForAnimationFrame</a>. On GHC it will delay
--   the execution of the current batch of asynchronous command when they
--   are sent to JavaScript. It will not delay the Haskell code execution.
--   The time returned will be based on the Haskell clock (not the
--   JavaScript clock).
waitForAnimationFrame :: JSM Double

-- | Tries to executes the given code in the next animation frame callback.
--   Avoid synchronous opperations where possible.
nextAnimationFrame :: (Double -> JSM a) -> JSM a
data AnimationFrameHandle

-- | Run the action in an animationframe callback. The action runs in a
--   synchronous thread, and is passed the high-performance clock time
--   stamp for that frame.
inAnimationFrame :: OnBlocked -> (Double -> JSM ()) -> JSM AnimationFrameHandle

-- | Run the action in an animationframe callback. The action runs in a
--   synchronous thread, and is passed the high-performance clock time
--   stamp for that frame. On GHCJS this version will continue
--   asynchronously if it is not possible to complete the callback
--   synchronously.
inAnimationFrame' :: (Double -> JSM ()) -> JSM AnimationFrameHandle

-- | Provide a handler for exceptions thrown during execution of the first
--   action. Note that type of the type of the argument to the handler will
--   constrain which exceptions are caught. See <a>Control.Exception</a>'s
--   <a>catch</a>.
catch :: (MonadCatch m, HasCallStack, Exception e) => m a -> (e -> m a) -> m a

-- | Generalized abstracted pattern of safe resource acquisition and
--   release in the face of errors. The first action "acquires" some value,
--   which is "released" by the second action at the end. The third action
--   "uses" the value and its result is the result of the <a>bracket</a>.
--   
--   If an error is thrown during the use, the release still happens before
--   the error is rethrown.
--   
--   Note that this is essentially a type-specialized version of
--   <a>generalBracket</a>. This function has a more common signature
--   (matching the signature from <a>Control.Exception</a>), and is often
--   more convenient to use. By contrast, <a>generalBracket</a> is more
--   expressive, allowing us to implement other functions like
--   <a>bracketOnError</a>.
bracket :: (HasCallStack, MonadMask m) => m a -> (a -> m c) -> (a -> m b) -> m b
